A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRL research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original continuous-control experiments, FAS comparisons, stochastic-timestep evaluations, and appendix results for latent SRL, randomized frame-skipping, and TempoRL.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results in Tables 2-4 and 7, the GPM comparison, and the experimental appendix figures.

M1.justification: The GRU actor, model-assisted policy training, critic training, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the latent-state extension are also retained.

E1.justification: The same 11 continuous-control tasks, four-environment GPM comparison, stochastic-timestep scenarios, and Walker2d latent-state experiment remain. No dataset, domain, or task scenario is added.

E2.justification: SAC, GPM, model-based online planning, TempoRL, and randomized SAC retain their roles in the corresponding comparisons. Removing standalone plots does not remove these comparators from the retained evaluations.

E3.justification: Training sequence lengths, actor update frequencies, FAS evaluation, uniformly sampled stochastic timesteps, and environment-specific budgets remain unchanged. The new experimental overview does not establish any protocol change.

E4.justification: Removing v3 Figure 5 eliminates the detailed Humanoid comparison of SRL and online-planning sensitivity to action-sequence length; Table 4 retains only their aggregate FAS comparison. Stochastic-timestep validation, latent-state analysis, and randomized frame-skipping analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-trial reporting for SAC/SRL, the same standard-deviation and standard-error conventions, and ten-seed TempoRL results. No repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: v4 removes the standalone Hopper and Humanoid results in v3 Figures 2 and 5. The Hopper curves differ numerically from the retained appendix curves, so their removal is not merely deduplication; the Humanoid online-planning curve is also absent. Tables 2-4 and 7 and the retained plot images are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(7), including the training losses and latent-space formulation, remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the claim that SRL replicates basal-ganglia action chunking. The central claims about model-based training, model-free sequence control, FAS, and comparative performance remain; biological inspiration is still discussed elsewhere.

C2.justification: v4 removes the hypothesis explaining GPM's limitations through disrupted sequence consistency and the future-work expectation of near-infinite-horizon control in noiseless environments. Existing modeling-error explanations and practical limitations remain. The neuroscience discussion is relocated, not deleted.

D1.justification: The new Section 5 overview explicitly identifies OpenAI Gym's MuJoCo implementation as the experimental platform, clarifying an existing setup without establishing a software change. Appendix hyperparameters, architectures, hardware, and repository information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Brockman et al. (2016), OpenAI Gym. The repaired OpenAI et al. (2019) citation refers to an already included work, and the relocated neuroscience discussion retains its references. Broader research positioning is substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds an experiments overview and appendix contents, promotes Hyperparameters to a numbered subsection, moves Neural Basis for Sequence Learning from Section 6 to Appendix A.9, and trims introductory and discussion passages. Most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 removes main-text Figures 2, 3, and 5, shrinks Figure 1, and repositions tables and appendix figures. The removed Ant scatterplot survives in the appendix. Retained graphics and table structures are largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves navigation and claim precision through the appendix contents, experimental overview, and removal of the abstract's biological-replication claim. The unchanged tables preserve central empirical support, although deleting distinct Hopper and Humanoid curves sacrifices result detail and limits the overall benefit.
